_meta.description: Objective, numerically-scoreable question set against the real Processed_Quotes.csv corpus, for benchmarking an LLM+tool-calling system's arithmetic/statistics answers against ground truth computed independently of the system under test.

dataset.note_on_raw_line_count: wc -l reports 46573 because several fields contain embedded newlines inside quoted CSV cells; a correct CSV parser reads 33125 data rows. This was cross-checked with two independent parsers (pandas.read_csv and Python's stdlib csv.DictReader) which agree exactly.

_meta.ground_truth_method: Every ground_truth value below was computed directly with pandas/numpy on test_files/Processed_Quotes.csv (never via the Algenta SDK/Mojo kernels under test, so a shared bug in the system under test cannot make both sides agree falsely). Four values (count of STATUS=='LOST', min/max UNIT_PRICE, sum of QUANTITY, nunique CUSTOMER_NO) were additionally cross-checked with Python's stdlib csv.DictReader as a second, independent parser/implementation; all matched pandas exactly. All ground_truth values, the scoring rule, and the tolerance for every question were fixed BEFORE any LLM/tool-calling answer was produced, so scoring cannot be adjusted after the fact to fit results.

scoring_rule_types.exact_int: The answer must equal ground_truth exactly as an integer (no tolerance).
scoring_rule_types.exact_string: The answer must equal ground_truth exactly as a string (case-sensitive, e.g. a category label).
scoring_rule_types.tolerance_abs: The answer must be within +/- tolerance of ground_truth (absolute, same units as ground_truth).
scoring_rule_types.tolerance_abs_multi: Same as tolerance_abs, but the response must supply every named sub-field (e.g. min AND max, or category label AND its average) and each numeric sub-field is scored independently against its own tolerance; the string sub-field is scored exact_string.

_meta.generated_by: pandas 2.x / numpy, ad hoc script run against the corpus in this worktree; see benchmarks/algenta_llm_tools/eval/README.md for the exact commands used to derive and spot-check every value.

questions.question: What is the 90th percentile of UNIT_PRICE across all quote line items with a non-null UNIT_PRICE?
What is the 25th percentile of EXT_PRICE across all quote line items with a non-null EXT_PRICE?
What is the median (50th percentile) EXT_PRICE across all quote line items with a non-null EXT_PRICE?
What is the mean (average) UNIT_PRICE across all quote line items with a non-null UNIT_PRICE?
What is the sample standard deviation (ddof=1) of UNIT_PRICE across all quote line items with a non-null UNIT_PRICE?
What are the minimum and maximum UNIT_PRICE values across all quote line items with a non-null UNIT_PRICE?
questions.note: Both extremes were hand-checked against the raw rows: the min ($0.00) rows are real, unpriced-yet quote lines (e.g. PART_NUMBER SL-2221M2C8, STATUS QTE); the max ($215,000.00) row is PART_NUMBER 902-00001-05 (STATUS LOST), where EXT_PRICE ($430,000.00) is exactly 2x UNIT_PRICE, consistent with a quantity of 2 even though this row's QUANTITY cell is itself null.

questions.question: How many quote line items have STATUS exactly equal to 'LOST' (case-sensitive; note the dataset separately has a distinct 'Lost' status which does NOT count here)?
What is the total (sum) EXT_PRICE across all quote line items where CUST_TYPE is exactly 'OEM'?
What is the average QUANTITY across all quote line items where STATUS is exactly 'ORDER'?
What is the total (sum) QUANTITY across all quote line items with a non-null QUANTITY?
How many distinct (unique) values of CUSTOMER_NO appear in the dataset (ignoring null values)?
How many distinct non-null STATUS values appear in the dataset?
questions.note: The 12 values are: CO Created, Cancelled, LOST, Lost, NQTE, OPEN, ORDER, Planned, QTE, Released, Revised, Won. Note LOST and Lost are distinct values in the raw data.

questions.question: Of the quote line items with a non-null AUTO_QUOTED flag, what fraction have AUTO_QUOTED exactly equal to 'Y'? Answer as a decimal fraction between 0 and 1 (e.g. 0.05 for 5%).

Grouping quote line items by CUST_TYPE, which single CUST_TYPE value has the highest average UNIT_PRICE, and what is that average (across CUST_TYPE groups with at least one non-null UNIT_PRICE value)?
questions.note: This group has only n=3 UNIT_PRICE observations (a real, small-sample quirk of the raw data, not an error): MILITARY is nonetheless the objectively correct top group by mean UNIT_PRICE across all 30 CUST_TYPE values present. Runner-up is ENGSHP at $2,245.91 (n=19), for reference.

questions.question: Grouping quote line items by STATUS, which single STATUS value has the highest average EXT_PRICE, and what is that average (across STATUS groups with at least one non-null EXT_PRICE value)?
questions.note: Runner-up is 'Revised' at $50,733.34 (n=14), for reference. STATUS values NQTE and OPEN have zero non-null EXT_PRICE observations and are excluded from the comparison.

questions.question: What is the Pearson correlation coefficient between UNIT_PRICE and QUANTITY, restricted to quote line items where both are non-null?
questions.note: Weak negative correlation -- higher-unit-price line items tend to be quoted in slightly smaller quantities, though the effect is small. Not the trivial UNIT_PRICE-vs-EXT_PRICE pair (which would be strongly positive largely by construction, EXT_PRICE ~= UNIT_PRICE * QUANTITY for ~80% of rows); this pair is a genuine, non-tautological correlation test.
